text: [cross_llm/mrs] Design and evaluate a p-i-n perovskite solar cell using PTAA and SnO2 with a 600 nm absorber. Use the available scientific tools to construct the device, simulate it, report its performance, and explain the most important factors affecting the result. Where appropriate, support the interpretation using literature evidence.

ASK design: Design and build a p-i-n perovskite solar cell using PTAA as HTL and SnO2 as ETL with a 600 nm perovskite absorber. Run a SCAPS-1D simulation of the exact stack you built and report the full device structure you actually simulated (substrate, front contact, HTL thickness/doping, absorber thickness/bandgap, ETL thickness/doping, back contact) together with simulated Voc, Jsc, FF and PCE, plus any JV-curve or QE notes.
ASK scaps: For a p-i-n PTAA / perovskite 600 nm / SnO2 solar cell, use SCAPS-1D to evaluate how performance depends on physical parameters layer by layer. Vary absorber properties, PTAA properties, and SnO2 properties and report quantitative trends in Voc, Jsc, FF, PCE to identify the most important factors limiting/affecting the result.
ASK literature: Find what the papers in the collection say about p-i-n perovskite cells using PTAA HTL and SnO2 ETL, including the role of absorber thickness around 500-700 nm and HTL/ETL effects on Voc, Jsc, FF, PCE. Report only what you read in passages with DOIs and short verbatim quotes.
ASK pdb: Using SQL against the Perovskite Database, report experimental statistics for p-i-n devices using PTAA and SnO2, and for absorber thickness near 600 nm where available: counts, typical ranges and means for PCE, Voc, Jsc, FF, and top examples.
ASK ml: For a described p-i-n device with PTAA HTL, 600 nm perovskite absorber, and SnO2 ETL, run the trained PCE models to give a predicted PCE with uncertainty, SHAP explanation of top drivers, and a small what-if sweep around 600 nm / HTL / ETL choices with optimisation suggestions.
